title: Capacity conversation cafe - ops notes (informal)
content:
Context: informal midweek 'conversation cafe' after standup. Goal: surface small ideas and low-cost experiments we can try this sprint to improve regional tail latency and reduce wasted warm tokens. Not a formal runbook update — raw notes and hypotheses.

Date: 2026-08-19
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Attendees: Ethan, Rashmi, Jonas, Priya (+ a few drop-ins from SRE shift)

High level summary:
- Short experiments proposed: lightweight cross-region slot borrowing prototype, model-family-specific prewarm windows, and an adaptive cheap-priming layer for cold long-context requests.
- Observed problem: 95th/99th latency spikes correlate with bursty long-context chat sessions (>=1024 tokens) in EU-west and APAC during peak minutes.
- Quick metric snapshot (from last 24h dashboards):
  - Global GPU slot fill: 78% avg, regional variance EU-west 91%, US-west 66%, APAC 72%
  - Queue wait median: 120 ms, 95th: 1.8 s, 99th: 3.6 s
  - Warm-token waste (estimate): 11.3% of tokens billed are from prewarm prefixes not used due to session truncation

Notes / raw observations:
- Jonas: EU-west burst pattern looks like a handful of customers running long chat threads during their morning. These sessions are sticky and take multiple GPU windows. The routing policy currently pins by customer which causes local saturation.
- Rashmi: We could allow ephemeral cross-region handoff for read-only inference (low-sensitivity customers) to smooth hits. Need to evaluate networking latency vs. priming cost.
- Ethan: Proposed prototype: 'borrowed slot' RSVP flow — if local queue > threshold and remote region has available slots and RTT < 80ms, move request with metadata (mark as borrowed). Fall back to pinned region if model-variant mismatch.
- Priya: We should be cautious with billing attribution and SLA messaging; borrowed slots change customer region visibility. Add a header to responses so customers can opt-in in beta.

Ideas & experiments (lightweight, rank-ordered):
1) Cheap-priming shim (2–4 tokens tokenized primer) for very long requests that typically cold-start KV caches. Hypothesis: small cheap primer reduces KV miss amplification and reduces downstream warm-token spend. Implementation: insert a zero-effect primer token pair (e.g., "​") at dispatch for sequences longer than 1024 tokens. Test on sample of 5 heavy customers. (Owner: Ethan)

2) Region-borrow MVP: allow non-sensitive routes to accept cross-region forwarding with RTT cutoff 80ms and cost threshold X (config flag). Add flags: allow_borrow, borrow_max_tps. Start with Canary customers only. (Owner: Jonas)

3) Model-family batch-sched shim: detect llama-family vs opt-family vs mix and use different max_batch_size and latency SLOs per family. Quick config toggle in balancer to test one family for 48h. (Owner: Rashmi)

4) Prewarm window heuristics: when a customer opens a session and sends short messages (<50 tokens) but later sends long messages, our current prewarming window is too short. Idea: keep a soft prefix cache per session for 2x previous max length or 30s whichever is larger. (Owner: Priya)

Risk notes / questions to escalate:
- Cross-region borrow introduces data residency/regulatory risks for enterprise customers. Need product gating and an allowlist. (Raised: Priya)
- Billing/usage attribution complexity for borrowed slots — finance needs to sign off on how to report inter-region cost. Add to JIRA-OPS-1987.
- Potential negative UX: slightly higher RTT for borrowed requests (if network unpredictable). Need to measure error/fallthrough rate.

Quick experiment design details (cheap-priming):
- Population: 5 identified heavy chat customers in EU-west (consent from customer support).
- Metric targets: reduce 99th token latency by >=10% and warm-token waste by >=5% within 7 days. Secondary: no regression on per-request generation quality (basic sampling-based sanity checks).
- Instrumentation: tag requests with header X-CP-PRIMER and emit per-session primer_used boolean to metrics.
- Rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for those customers after success checks.

Operational runbook snippets (temporary):
- If borrower fails RTT check or model mismatch: fallback to original region with logging event BORROW_FAIL_{reason}. Alert at BORROW_FAIL rate > 1% per minute for canary set.
- If priming causing hallucination or tokenization breaks (edge cases with non-printable primers), auto-kill primer flow and revert config. Add guard: primer tokens must be in UTF-8 safe set.

Action items (owner, by-date):
- Ethan: implement cheap-priming shim prototype + instrumentation (due 2026-08-25)
- Jonas: prototype borrow flow in balancer (read-only alpha) + test harness for RTT gating (due 2026-08-27)
- Rashmi: prepare model-family batching toggle and run 48h experiment on opt-family traffic (due 2026-08-24)
- Priya: write product note and permission gating for borrowed slots; draft opt-in header semantics (due 2026-08-23)
- Maya: coordinate with customer-support to reach out to the 5 heavy customers for consent to test cheap primer (due 2026-08-20)

Open questions to discuss next standup:
- How do we measure 'warm-token waste' precisely across multi-tenant caches? Is there an existing metric we can repurpose?
- Should borrowed slot be a first-class routing policy or an emergency backstop only?
- How to communicate trial features to enterprise customers while keeping SLA promises?

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider adding an 'economics leash' to borrowed slots: only borrow if estimated net cost per token lower than local prewarm cost + expected latency penalty.
- Small thought: if we add cheap-priming globally, agree on token content that is Unicode invisible and robust in different tokenizers. Might need tokenizer tests across top-6 models.

Relevant links & references:
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-1987 (billing attribution for cross-region flow)
- Confluence: priming strategies (internal draft) https://confluence.redwood.team/pages/priming-strategies-2026
- Slack channel: #gpu-ops for immediate followups

Closing: informal session was productive — we have 3 small low-risk experiments to try this sprint. We'll reconvene in async thread with early telemetry and decide whether to continue or revert.

---
Raw appendices (telemetry snippets grabbed in meeting):
1) EU-west heavy session sample (timestamps omitted for PII):
   - 4 sessions > 1200 tokens in 20-min window -> local queue 2.1x baseline, 99p latency 3.9s
2) Sample log line for BORROW_FAIL: {event: BORROW_FAIL, reason: MODEL_MISMATCH, origin_region: eu-west, target_region: us-east, rtt_ms: 102} (we'll add structured schema later)

End of notes.
